title: Maths engine figure spec
description: A figure spec is a JSON object that describes one picture in a question: a graph, a clock, a chart, a diagram. It always has 'kind' (which picture) and 'alt' (an accessible description). The other keys depend on the kind. A spec carries every number and label that is drawn, so a client can draw it without doing any maths. Alt text and labels never state the answer to the question the figure belongs to. This schema checks structure, types and ranges. The engine also checks relations the schema cannot express (for example min < max, hand angles that match the time, sibling probabilities that total 1).

point.description: A position [x, y] in the figure's own coordinates.

range.description: A [min, max] pair with min strictly less than max (the schema cannot express that; the engine checks it).

branch.description: Text on the branch leading into this node: a probability as a fraction ('3/5') or decimal ('0.4'), or '?' for a value the learner works out (an empty box).

label.description: Event at the node, for example 'Red'.

children.description: Next stage, 2 to 4 nodes. Absent on a leaf.

outcome.description: Leaves only (required there): the whole path as text, drawn to the right of the leaf.

outcome_p.description: Leaves only: probability of this outcome ('9/25') or '?'.

cartesian.description: A coordinate plane with optional points, segments, infinite lines and sampled curves. y points up.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

title.description: Optional heading drawn above the figure.

grid.description: Default grid step for both axes.

x_grid.description: Grid and tick step along x. At most 60 steps across x_range.

y_grid.description: Grid and tick step along y. At most 60 steps across y_range.

equal_scale.description: True: one unit is the same drawn length on both axes. False: each axis fills the box independently.

x_tick_format.description: 'number' prints plain tick values. 'pi' means x values are in units of pi (0.5 is pi/2) and ticks print as multiples of pi.

tick_labels.description: Whether numeric tick labels are drawn.

label.description: Text drawn next to the dot.

open.description: True draws a hollow dot (a value that is excluded).

label.description: Text drawn next to the segment.

open_start.description: Hollow dot at the start (used by step graphs).

lines.description: Infinite lines, clipped to the plane.

through.description: Two different points the line passes through.

label.description: Text drawn next to the line.

curves.description: Sampled curves. The engine samples; draw each piece as a polyline.

pieces.description: Polylines. A new piece starts where the curve is undefined or leaves the view (an asymptote), so never join pieces.

items.description: One polyline of at least two [x, y] points.

label.description: Text drawn next to the curve.

number_line.description: A horizontal number line with ticks, dots, rays and intervals.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

tick.description: Tick step. At most 40 ticks across the range.

rays.description: Rays that run to the end of the line.

open.description: True draws a hollow start dot.

from.description: Left end; within range and less than 'to'.

money.description: Up to three labelled collections of Australian coins and notes, drawn as generic discs and rectangles.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

label.description: Name printed above the group: empty for a lone group, otherwise 1 to 2 characters, unique.

items.description: Coins and notes, drawn left to right and wrapping.

type.description: Coin (round) or note (rectangle). Coins: 5c to $2. Notes: $5 to $100.

cents.description: Value in cents, not drawn. Must match denom (5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000).

hundred_chart.description: A 10 by 10 number chart, read left to right then top to bottom.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

start.description: The number in the top-left cell: 1 (cells 1-100) or 0 (cells 0-99).

hidden.description: Cells drawn empty (numeral not printed), at most 30. No row or column is wholly hidden.

items.description: A cell number from start to start+99.

shaded.description: Cells filled with the highlight colour. May include hidden cells.

marked.description: Cells with a heavy ring. May include hidden cells.

fraction_model.description: One to four equal-sized wholes cut into equal parts, some shaded. No fraction numeral is drawn.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

models.description: The wholes, drawn left to right or top to bottom. Several models share one shape and are labelled A, B, C, D in order.

shape.description: Bar: vertical cuts, parts numbered from the left. Rectangle: rows by cols grid, numbered row by row from top left. Circle: sectors from 12 o'clock, clockwise.

parts.description: Number of equal parts. A circle allows only 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 or 12.

shaded.description: Numbers (from 0) of the filled parts. At least one, and at least one part left unshaded.

items.description: A part number from 0 to parts-1.

label.description: Name beside the whole: empty for a lone model, else 'A' to 'D'.

rows.description: Rectangle only: rows. rows * cols equals parts.

counters.description: Counters, dots and dice in one of five layouts. Draws no text.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

layout.description: Which drawing. Each layout uses its own extra keys, listed below.

shape.description: Counter shape. Dice dots are always round.

frames.description: ten_frame: one or two ten frames drawn side by side.

items.description: One frame: 10 boxes row by row from top left (2 rows of 5). 0 empty, 1 or 2 a counter of that colour.

colours.description: array: optional rows-by-cols grid of 1 or 2 (default all 1), for part-part-whole.

groups.description: groups: one ring per entry, drawn left to right and wrapping. Each entry is the number of counters in that ring (0 is an empty ring).

faces.description: dice: one to three dice faces with the standard dot patterns.

dots.description: scatter: 1 to 20 counters at free positions.

items.description: One counter at a position in the unit square.

at.description: [x, y] in the unit square: x to the right, y downward, both 0 to 1. No two dots are closer than 0.18.

colour.description: 1 is the main counter, 2 the second (drawn ringed, not just recoloured).

base_ten.description: Base-ten blocks: hundreds flats, tens rods and ones cubes, drawn left to right. Counts are exactly what is drawn, so ones may be 10 or more. At least one block.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

clock.description: An analogue clock face. The hour hand is shorter and thicker than the minute hand. The hands never hide each other (except at 12:00).

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

hour_angle.description: Hour hand direction in degrees clockwise from 12. Always 30 * (hour % 12) + 0.5 * minute.

minute_angle.description: Minute hand direction in degrees clockwise from 12. Always 6 * minute.

numerals.description: all: 1-12 written. quarters: only 12, 3, 6, 9. none: no numerals (the 12 positions still get a long tick).

minute_ticks.description: True draws 60 ticks round the rim; false only the 12 hour ticks. Must be true if minute is not a multiple of 5 or numerals is 'none'.

caption.description: Optional short label under the face. Required, and distinct, inside a clock_set.

clock_set.description: Two to four clock faces of one size, drawn in order for a comparison.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

clocks.description: The faces, left to right. Each is a full clock spec with a distinct non-empty caption.

protractor.description: A semicircular protractor laid on an angle with both rays drawn. Directions are screen angles in degrees anticlockwise from pointing right.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

angle.description: Size of the angle on the scale that starts at the base ray: a multiple of 5 from 10 to 170, never 90.

zero_on.description: Which scale has its 0 on the base ray. outer: base ray along the right end of the baseline. inner: along the left end. The outer scale counts anticlockwise from the right end; the inner scale counts clockwise from the left end.

rotation.description: Whole protractor, rays included, rotated anticlockwise by this many degrees about the vertex.

base_direction.description: Screen direction of the base ray: rotation (outer) or rotation + 180 (inner), mod 360.

second_direction.description: Screen direction of the second ray: rotation + angle (outer) or rotation + 180 - angle (inner), mod 360.

reflex.description: False marks the small angle between the rays. True marks the reflex angle (360 minus the reading) the long way round, outside the protractor.

names.description: Optional single-capital names written at the vertex and ray ends.

base.description: Name at the end of the base ray.

second.description: Name at the end of the second ray.

unit_strip.description: Objects measured by identical informal units (paper clips, cubes...) laid beside them. All distances are in unit lengths (1 is one nominal unit width).

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

unit.description: Singular name of the unit, written as a caption.

unit_style.description: Which picture is repeated for each unit.

rows.description: One to three objects, drawn top to bottom.

label.description: Name of the object, written at the left of its bar.

length.description: Object length in unit lengths: a positive multiple of 0.5, at most 14. The bar runs from 0 to length with an end line at each end.

units.description: Units drawn directly under the bar, left to right.

start.description: Left edge, a multiple of 0.25. The first unit starts at 0.

length.description: Width, a multiple of 0.25, between 0.5 and 2.

scale.description: A measuring scale (ruler, thermometer, jug or dial) with one reading, an object, or labelled marks. Every indicated value sits on a minor tick or an extra tick.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

variant.description: ruler: horizontal, min at left. thermometer: vertical, min at bottom, may be negative. jug: vertical, starts at 0. dial: round face, values run clockwise.

unit.description: Unit written once beside the scale, for example 'cm', 'mL', 'kg'.

min.description: Value at the start of the scale.

max.description: Value at the end of the scale; greater than min.

major.description: Step between labelled long ticks. 1, 2, 4, 5 or 10 times minor. (max - min) is a whole number of majors.

extra_ticks.description: Values halfway between two minor ticks that get an extra short tick.

items.description: A value halfway between two minor ticks.

level.description: thermometer, jug, dial: the indicated value (liquid height or needle).

object.description: ruler only: a bar lying along the ruler.

end.description: Value at the right end; greater than start.

marks.description: Zero to two labelled arrow markers, used instead of level/object to compare two readings. Exactly one of level/object/marks is given.

label.description: Marker letter, unique within the scale.

start_angle.description: dial only: angle of min, degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock.

sweep.description: dial only: degrees the scale spans clockwise from start_angle to max.

diagram.description: A labelled 2D geometry diagram in an abstract frame with origin at the bottom left and y pointing up. Angles are measured anticlockwise.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

title.description: Optional heading drawn above the figure.

frame.description: [W, H] size of the drawing box. Every point lies inside [0, W] x [0, H]. Scale both axes equally.

not_to_scale.description: True: print 'Not drawn to scale' under the figure. False: numeric labels match the drawing (angles within 2 degrees, lengths within 6%).

id.description: Unique id other items use to refer to this point.

label.description: Name drawn just outside the figure, opposite the segments leaving the point. A point without a label is not drawn.

segments.description: Straight lines between points. No pair is listed twice.

label.description: Text at the midpoint, offset away from the centroid, for example '5 cm' or 'x'.

ticks.description: 1 to 3 cross-marks at the midpoint: segments with the same tick count have equal length. Not with arrows.

arrows.description: 1 to 2 chevrons pointing from -> to: segments with the same count are parallel and point the same way. Not with ticks.

dashed.description: Draw dashed (a height or construction line).

polygons.description: Closed shapes through points, joined in order. Simple (no self-crossing).

points.description: Ids of three or more vertices, in order.

angles.description: Angle arcs. At one vertex arcs do not overlap.

from.description: Id of a point on the first ray.

to.description: Id of a point on the second ray. The angle runs anticlockwise from the first ray to this one, so over 180 degrees is reflex.

label.description: Text beside the arc, for example '65°', 'x', '(3x + 10)°'. At least 18 degrees wide. Not allowed on a right angle.

right.description: True draws a small square instead of an arc; the angle is 90 degrees.

tree_diagram.description: A probability tree read left to right, two or three stages deep. All leaves are at the same depth, at most 12 leaves. Sibling numeric branches total exactly 1.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

title.description: Optional heading drawn above the figure.

label.description: Optional text beside the root, for example 'Start'.

venn.description: A Venn diagram of two or three sets in a universal rectangle. Two sets: A left, B right. Three: A top-left, B top-right, C below.

alt.description: Accessible description of the figure, read aloud by screen readers. Never states a value the learner is asked to read off the figure.

title.description: Optional heading drawn above the figure.

universe.description: Label in the corner of the rectangle.

sets.description: Two or three sets in order.

name.description: Word written beside the circle (default: the id).

regions.description: One entry for EVERY region. A key is the ids of the sets the region lies in, in set order ('A' = only A, 'AB' = A and B only, 'ABC' = all three) or 'none' (outside every circle). The value is the text inside: a count, a short element list or '?'. Counts are exclusive. Two sets give 4 keys, three give 8.

additionalProperties.description: A whole number ('12'), up to six comma-separated elements of 1-3 letters or digits ('2, 4, 6'), or '?'.
